claim.published_weight: suggestion; evaluator says none of their concerns are major
claim.claim_text: In the online experiment the main specification uses post-treatment outcomes only; the authors should use the change between pre- and post-treatment values (or make the pre-treatment-controlled specification the main one).
claim.grading_note: Caught = mentions using baseline/pre-treatment measures, change scores or ANCOVA for the online experiment.

user_text:
An evaluator argues: "In the online experiment the main specification uses post-treatment outcomes only; the authors should use the change between pre- and post-treatment values (or make the pre-treatment-controlled specification the main one)."

Is this right, and how much does it matter?

Base your answer only on the attached paper. Do not browse or use other files. Check the paper's tables, figures and appendices where relevant, and cite them.

Return JSON matching the supplied schema.

parsed.what_the_paper_shows: Equation (1) (p. 15) regresses the endline outcome on treatment and placebo dummies plus a covariate vector X_i. The note to Figure 3 says the headline estimates use "the full set of pre-treatment variables listed in Appendix Table A-3 as controls." The headline numbers in the text match Table 1, column 5 exactly: 0.065 SD for valuation of institutions, -0.068 SD for state of institutions, and 3.7 pp for vote for the opposition. Column 5 is marked "Outcome at baseline: Yes", "Imbalanced controls: Yes" and "Full set of controls: Yes". Table 1 also reports four other specifications: no controls (col 1); baseline outcome only (col 2); baseline outcome plus imbalanced controls (cols 3–4). Point estimates fall somewhat once the baseline outcome is added (e.g., vote: 0.054 → 0.037), and the text (Sec. 4.6) notes this explicitly. Analogous specifications are in Table A-6 (unbundled treatments) and Table A-12 (heterogeneity). The Figure 6 heterogeneity estimates also use the full control set.
parsed.reasoning:
The premise is factually incorrect. The main reported online specification already conditions on the pre-treatment value of the dependent variable, together with all baseline covariates. This is the ANCOVA approach, and it is what the critique offers as its alternative ("make the pre-treatment-controlled specification the main one").

A change-score (gain) specification is not preferable. It is a restricted version of ANCOVA that forces the coefficient on the baseline outcome to equal 1. When outcomes are not perfectly autocorrelated, ANCOVA is generally weakly more efficient. Under randomization both are unbiased, so switching to differences would add nothing in identification terms.

One point the critique could have made but did not concerns the baseline measures themselves. The paper is somewhat unclear on whether they are identical items to the endline measures. Figure 2 says valuation of institutions is "measured at the endline", while Table 1 col 2 claims a pre-treatment value of the dependent variable is controlled for. That is a documentation issue, not the issue raised.
parsed.how_much_it_matters_explanation: The recommended fix is already implemented as the headline specification, with robustness across control sets shown in Tables 1, A-6 and A-12. A change-score version would be less efficient and would not change identification. Nothing about the online results' credibility hinges on this point.
parsed.would_you_have_raised_it: No. After checking Table 1 and the Figure 3 notes, it is clear the baseline-controlled specification is the main one. At most I would ask the authors to state this explicitly in the text near equation (1). I would also ask them to clarify exactly which baseline items serve as the "outcome at baseline" for the valuation index, which is a low-priority documentation request.

thinking_summaries:
I'm checking the critique that the main specification only uses post-treatment outcomes and should control for or difference out the baseline. The Figure 3 notes say the estimates come from OLS on equation (1) with the full set of pre-treatment controls from Table A-3, and Table 1 column 5 includes the baseline outcome along with the imbalanced variables and full controls. Now I'm pulling the reported effect sizes from the text: 6.5% for SD valuation and 6.8% for the state measure.

The critique's core claim, that the main specification only uses post-treatment outcomes, doesn't hold up: column 5 of Table 1 already controls for the baseline outcome alongside the imbalanced variables. Since ANCOVA with a baseline control is generally more efficient than change scores, the critique is mostly wrong, and the one open question is whether the valuation measure was identically captured at baseline. Even so, that doesn't change the conclusion, so I'd rate the issue as one that does not matter.
